title: Application (24A846) to extend the time to file a petition for a writ of certiorari from April 3, 2025 to June 2, 2025, submitted to Justice Barrett

pages.text:
No. _______
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES
SHAWN MONTGOMERY,
Petitioner,
v.
CARIBE TRANSPORT II, LLC,
YOSNIEL VARELA-MOJENA,
C.H. ROBINSON WORLDWIDE, INC.,
C.H. ROBINSON COMPANY,
C.H. ROBINSON COMPANY, INC.,
C.H. ROBINSON INTERNATIONAL, INC.,
and CARIBE TRANSPORT, LLC,
Respondents.
APPLICATION FOR EXTENSION OF TIME
TO FILE PETITION FOR WRIT OF CERTIORARI TO THE
UNITED STATES COURT OF APPEALS
FOR THE SEVENTH CIRCUIT
To the Honorable Amy Coney Barrett , Circuit Justice for the Seventh
Circuit:
Under Supreme Court Rule 13.5, Petitioner Shawn Montgomery
requests an extension of time to petition for a writ of certiorari. Petitioner
requests a 60 -day extension of time through Monday, June 2, 2025 .
The decision in the Seventh Circuit was entered on January 3, 2025, and
the time to file a petition for writ of certiorari in this Court will expire on

2

April 3, 2025. This application is being filed more than 10 days before the
due date.
Attached to this application is a copy of the decision below. See
Exhibit A. This Court would have jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1254(1).
Below, the Seventh  Circuit held that the Federal Aviation
Administration Authorization Act of 1994 preempts state law claims that
a freight broker negligently hired a motor carrier. The Seventh Circuit’s
decision aligns with the Eleventh Circuit’s decisions in Aspen American
Insurance Co. v. Landstar Ranger, Inc. , 65 F.4th 1261 (11th Cir. 2023),
and Gauthier v. Hard to Stop LLC, No. 22-10774, 2024 WL 3338944 (11th
Cir. July 9, 2024).
The Seventh and Eleventh Circuit’s decisions conflict with the
Ninth Circuit’s decision in Miller v. C.H. Robinson Worldwide, Inc., 976
F.3d 1016 (9th Cir. 2020). The Ninth Circuit held that a safety-exception
in the Act means that such claims are not preempted.
The reason for the requested extension of time is the pendency of a
Sixth Circuit appeal, which could deepen the circuit conflict. See Cox v.
Total Quality Logistics, Inc. , No. 24 -3599 (6th Cir.) (oral argument

3

occurred on January 29, 2025). An extension is also necessary due to the
press of other business.
Respondents do not oppose Petitioner’s requested extension of time
to file his Petition for Writ of Certiorari.
Respectfully submitted,

Bryan S. Gowdy
